hints: Look closely at the grey muscle around W and X. Which cavity is surrounded by much thicker muscle, and which cavity looks like a thin crescent or slit?
Remember which ventricle pumps blood all the way around the body and needs a very thick wall, compared to the ventricle that only pumps a short distance to the lungs.
walkthrough:
**Spot that this is a transverse section of the ventricles**

This is a cross-section through the lower pumping chambers, not the upper atria. You can tell because both cavities are surrounded by thick grey muscle, which is ventricular wall muscle.

Atria have very thin walls, so they would not look like this.

**Compare muscle thickness and cavity shape**

Look at X. It has a large cavity and is surrounded by very thick grey muscle, especially below. Look at W. It has a small, slit-like cavity and a much thinner outer wall.

Rule to remember: left ventricle wall is about 3 times thicker than right ventricle wall because it generates much higher pressure.

**Link structure to function and identify W and X**

The left ventricle pumps blood to the whole body, so it needs thick muscle. The right ventricle only pumps to the nearby lungs, so it has thinner muscle and often a crescent shape that wraps around the left.

Therefore X with the thick wall is the left ventricle, and W with the thin wall is the right ventricle.

options.A: Reversed. W has the thinner wall so cannot be the left ventricle, and X has the thicker wall so cannot be the right ventricle.
options.B: Incorrect, as both cavities are surrounded by thick ventricular muscle, not the thin walls of the right and left atria.
options.C: Incorrect, as neither cavity is an atrium. W is a ventricle with a thin wall, specifically the right ventricle.
options.D: Correct. W is the right ventricle with thinner wall and small lumen, and X is the left ventricle with very thick wall and larger lumen.
